# Realtime Robotics Names Kevin Carlin CEO To Lead Next Phase Of Growth By Amit Chowdhry Today at 10:48 PM Realtime Robotics has appointed Kevin Carlin as Chief Executive Officer as the industrial AI company moves into its next phase of commercial growth and expands adoption of its Resolver platform among major automotive manufacturers\. Carlin succeeds Realtime Robotics Co-Founder Peter Howard, who will remain involved with the company as non-executive Chairman of the Board\. The leadership transition comes as Realtime Robotics reports growing adoption of Resolver among global automotive OEMs seeking to use AI to streamline factory planning, shorten vehicle development timelines, manage increasingly complex production environments, and accelerate the deployment of robotic manufacturing systems\. Realtime Robotics has also expanded its workforce while continuing to develop Resolver’s capabilities, positioning the company to scale its commercial operations as more manufacturers incorporate AI into production planning and automation\. Carlin brings more than two decades of international leadership experience across semiconductors, industrial automation, and artificial intelligence\.

# Microsoft previews MAI-Realtime bidirectional voice model Microsoft is quietly building its own voice AI stack, and the latest addition is MAI-Realtime, a bidirectional voice model currently in preview that the company says will deliver more natural interactions across multiple languages and tool integrations\. Bidirectional voice means the model can handle both speaking and listening simultaneously, rather than taking turns like a walkie-talkie\. The model processes audio in real time, going both directions at once, which is what makes voice feel genuinely conversational rather than robotic\. MAI-Realtime is currently in an internal preview phase, meaning Microsoft hasn’t opened it to public testing or released performance benchmarks yet\. What the company has confirmed is that the model is designed to feel more natural, support multiple languages, and work alongside tools, which in Microsoft’s ecosystem likely means integration with Copilot and the broader suite of productivity applications\. # Aborted plan for life-like robot in NY classroom alarms state teachers union An aborted plan to use a life-like robotic teacher’s assistant in a Western New York school district has prompted the state teacher’s union to call for new limits on artificial intelligence in schools\. Sally, a brunette, silicone-skinned android powered by AI, was set to debut this fall in Salamanca’s high school\. The town has a population of around 6,000 people and is part of the Allegany Indian Reservation, less than three hours from Cleveland\. The robot was to have been manufactured by Realbotix, which has a sibling company that produces sex dolls\. But after a public outcry and concern from State Education Commissioner Betty Rosa, the Salamanca school district put the plan on pause\. Melinda Person, president of the New York State Teachers Union, argued there were still lessons to be learned from the futuristic episode\. # Jupiter Hospital conducts first robotic kidney transplant outside China Mumbai: Jupiter Hospital, Thane, said it had successfully performed the world's first robotic kidney transplant surgeries outside China using the CE-certified Toumai robotic surgical system from MicroPort MedBot\. The Toumai robotic platform provided high-definition, three-dimensional visualisation with enhanced dexterity, precision and surgical control, supporting the surgical team in performing the highly complex transplant procedures, the hospital said\. The two consecutive transplants were carried out on patients with end-stage kidney disease, both of whom recovered well after surgery, the hospital added\.
